g_051510a2600e.description: Add a simple config module to read settings

g_a98ca3967525.description: Create a new config module with a load_config function that reads settings from a config.json file and returns them as a dictionary. Include default values if the file is missing.

tasks.action: Create a new config module with a load_config function that reads settings from a config.json file and returns them as a dictionary. Include default values if the file is missing.
tasks.interface_contract: Called at application startup to retrieve a settings dictionary; safe to call multiple times
constraints: Must return a dict in all cases, never None
Must provide default values if config.json does not exist
Must handle JSON decode errors gracefully by returning defaults
Default dict must include at least keys: 'debug' (bool, False), 'log_level' (str, 'INFO'), 'app_name' (str, 'MyApp')
must_not: Must not raise an exception if the file is missing or malformed
Must not use global mutable state or module-level side effects
Must not import from utils.py or main.py

g_7331edca3138.description: Import load_config from config module and call it inside the existing main function, storing the result in a local variable named 'settings', then print the app_name value from settings.

tasks.action: Import load_config from config module and call it inside the existing main function, storing the result in a local variable named 'settings', then print the app_name value from settings.
tasks.interface_contract: Entry point of the application; now initializes config before other logic
constraints: Must call load_config() as the first statement inside main()
Must store result in a variable named 'settings'
Must preserve any existing logic already inside main()
must_not: Must not call load_config() at module level outside of main()
Must not hardcode any config values
Must not remove or alter the existing import of format_string from utils
